verdict: Caterpillar's sales rose 17% to $20.7B on higher equipment volume and prices, and operating profit jumped 38% as those extra sales dropped through at much better margins.

segments.name: Machinery, Power & Energy
segments.note: The equipment businesses: Power & Energy $8,784M (+18%), Construction Industries $7,983M (+18%) and Resource Industries (mining) $4,615M (+15%), less corporate items and eliminations. Higher sales volume added $2.2B and better prices $663M.

segments.name: Financial Products
segments.note: Cat Financial — loans and leases that help customers and dealers buy and rent Caterpillar equipment.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Sales teams, dealers support and running the company — roughly flat YoY despite 17% sales growth.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Developing new machines, engines and technology — up 7% YoY.

opex.name: Interest expense of Financial Products
opex.note: The funding cost of Cat Financial's loan and lease book — the finance arm's equivalent of a cost of borrowing.

opex.name: Other operating expenses
opex.note: Other operating costs, net — more than double a year ago, partly offset in operating profit by $128M of tariff (IEEPA) recoveries.

otherDetail: Other income of $135M, less $129M of interest expense on non-financial debt, plus $34M of equity earnings from affiliated companies and a $1M noncontrolling-interest adjustment — net +$41M.
oneTimers: Restructuring costs of $41M before tax ($32M after tax, $0.07 per share) are included in GAAP results. Excluding them, adjusted EPS was $7.20 instead of $7.13.
Operating profit included $128M of IEEPA tariff recoveries — money back on tariffs previously paid — which flattered the 20.4% operating margin.

takeaways.title: Volume, not just price
takeaways.text: Sales rose $3.0B to $20.7B. About $2.2B of that was selling more equipment to end users and $663M was higher prices — demand, led by a record backlog, did most of the work.

takeaways.title: Margins expanded sharply
takeaways.text: Operating profit rose 38% to $4,214M and the operating margin widened to 20.4% from 17.3% a year ago, as the extra volume spread fixed costs — even with higher material and tariff costs in mining.

takeaways.title: Cash went back to shareholders
takeaways.text: Caterpillar returned $2.0B in the quarter — $1.2B of share buybacks and $0.7B of dividends — and ended the quarter with $7.9B of enterprise cash.
